title: GC7 combined grant - Title: Focused and differentiated TB/HIV prevention and treatment in Sudan
description: UNDP Sudan is the Principal Recipient for the Global Fund Grants for Tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS, COVID-19 Response Mechanism (C19RM) and support to implementation of Malaria grants. The projects objectives are to ensure continuation of essential TB and HIV services during the Sudan Emergency situation 2024-206, provide operational support to revamp build resilient and sustainable systems for health, strengthen community systems and mitigate COVID-19 impact on primary health care services. -	In line with the Sudan’s National Strategic Plans for HIV and TB (2022-2026), the strategies adopted during the implementation period of these projects are the following: -	 Coverage of quality ART services increased from 22.5% in 2023 to 28% in 2026.-	Coverage of key populations with the integrated package of HIV preventive and treatment services increased from 57% (MSM) and 38%(FSWs) in 2022 to 60% in 2026 (Both MSM and FSW)-	To increase TB treatment success rate from 83% in 2022 to 90% in 2026.-	To increase the detection of MDR/RR-TB from 135 in 2022 to 198 by 2026 and the treatment success rate from 73% in 2022 to 86% in 2026.-	To strengthen and upgrade the capacities of TB laboratory network; to maintain at least 183 functional microscopy centers, 1 culture zonal laboratories and to expand the number of GeneXpert sites to 60 by 2026. Projects activities will include the following: -	Supporting identification of presumptive TB and refer to the TB diagnostic and treatment facilities; conduct training on microscopy and HIV testing in the 9 stable states; Conduct Super user training on GeneXpert and quality of the GX services; train lab staff on use of TB TrueNat and provide communication cost for TBMUs; -	Integrated testing of pregnant women for HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B through advocacy and sensitization sessions for both RH and AIDS programs and Care Providers at high priority States integrated testing of pregnant women for HIV, Syphilis and Hepatitis B

title: Sudan Emergency and Famine Response Intuitive (SEFRI)
description: Sudan is witnessing the largest man-made crisis in its history that continues to spiral the country into chaos, The conflict that started between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) is having a horrific toll on civilians and leading to a humanitarian crisis of significant proportions that keeps worsening. The war has caused unprecedented widespread displacement, with over 8.8 million people fleeing their homes, including an estimated 6.8 million internally displaced persons (IDPs). UN famine prevention plan highlighted the gravity of the crisis, noting that immediate action is crucial to prevent a catastrophic hunger crisis. The nutrition situation, especially among children, has worsened, with recent surveys indicating a decline compared to the previous five years. The country is facing acute food insecurity, with 17.7 million people affected and 4.9 million on the verge of famine. An integrated response is urgently needed to address the vulnerabilities and restore normalcy in terms of lives, livelihoods, basic services, and economic opportunities. Tailoring solutions to the specific context of the affected areas is essential to enhance the resilience of IDPS and host communities against current and future shocks. UNDP role in providing support and assistance is vital in averting a potential famine and stabilizing the situation in Sudan.

title: Sudan Integrated Community Resilience Initiative (SIRI)
description: The Sudan Integrated Community Resilience Initiative (SIRI) is UNDP Sudan’s flagship on community resilience under the Resilience and Recovery Pillar. The Resilience and Recovery Pillar within the UNDP Sudan aspires to build the adaptative capacities of crises-affected communities to prevent, manage and recovery efficiently from disasters and to thrive. Our programming adopts the principles of Area-based integrated programming that enable the people of Sudan identify threats and anticipate risk and to draw on a range of assets, services and capabilities that enable them prevent, eliminate or reduce the impact of disaster on them and to recover efficiently with limited external support.

title: Sudan Pathways to Peace
description: Describe the main project goal; do not list outcomes and outputs (max 500 words)Sudan: Pathways to Peace aims to contribute to the country’s return to a peaceful future through a bottom-up conflict transformation strategy complementary to other existing tracks towards peace. In-depth analysis of conflict dynamics including conflict causes will allow for programmatic interventions that directly address and mitigate conflict drivers (historical and current), reducing violence and preventing conflict from escalating. Inclusive, community-owned dialogue processes of decision-making, prioritization, and ownership over solutions to conflict causes will contribute to peaceful co-existence within communities facing social cleavages and increasing tribal and ethnic polarization. Equally, systematic support to community-owned peace initiatives translating into localized ceasefire agreements brokered by civilian actors will contribute to sustaining and gradually expanding peace pockets through a bottom-up approach, while being fully cognisant and complementary of other peace tracks. Local agreements on power- and resource-sharing, on parameters for peaceful co-existence and the cessation of hostilities need to inform high-level mediation efforts of both ceasefire and political tracks, while track-1 decisions equally require translation into local conflict dynamics. The project will proactively build these bridges between Sudan’s communal peace infrastructure and the agenda-setting for, and participation in high-level fora outside the country aimed at determining the future of the Sudanese state. To this end, the project will focus on strategic locations in River Nile State (Atbara) and Central Darfur (Zalingei) with conditions conducive for the outlined work.

title: Enhancing accountability in Sudan to contribute to ending the cycles of violence and building sustainable peace
description: With atrocities against the civilian population, particularly women and children, being perpetrated on a massive scale in Sudan since the outbreak of the 2023 war, strengthening timely and meaningful accountability efforts is critical. In early 2024, UNITAMS transition discussion recognized the importance of the UN Country Team’s continued engagements toward accountability. These discussions resulted in a UNCT agreement to develop a holistic, cross-cutting approach to empowering and supporting civilian actors advocating for accountability as an essential component of Sudan’s return to peace. This project thus seeks to support community-based engagement in the protection of human rights and enable access to justice for victims and survivors of human rights violations – with particular emphasis on women and children. The proposal demonstrates OHCHR, UNDP, UNICEF, and UNODC’s shared commitment to jointly addressing protection challenges and barriers in accessing justice faced by vulnerable groups. The proposal follows the new UN country team’s common approach centred on civil society engagement, with the aim to strengthen foundations for accountability for human rights violations and abuses in Sudan

title: Promoting Spaces for Conflict Prevention and Reduced Vulnerability in Abyei:  A Joint Programme of the RCs in Sudan and South Sudan in Abyei (hereafter the  UN Joint Programme in Abyei
description: Briefly describe the overall development challenge and the expected results of the project.One year after the outbreak of the conflict in Sudan, more than 17,000 South Sudanese returnees have crossed into Abyei Administrative Area (Abyei AA), some with intentions of heading to South Sudan or to return to their respective communities once the security situation allows. While most of the population has moved on to South Sudan, a significant number of these people have remained in Abyei, where they have family ties including because of proximity. In addition, as of May 2024, close to 18,000 members of the Misseriya tribe, driven by conflict have crossed into Abyei, where they have remained and settled in the Northern part of Abyei. At the same time, close to 4,000 displaced persons, including refugees, mostly of Eritrean and Somali origin have crossed into Abyei from different parts of Sudan and settled into communities with no support. Due to the disputed nature of the Abyei AA there is a heightened sense of marginalization and exclusion dramatically exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in Sudan and instability in South Sudan. Access to the northern part of the box from Sudan has become more challenging, with the disruption of air corridors due to the war and the subsequent limited humanitarian assistance. While development and peacebuilding activities remain challenging in the north, due to the unresolved political complexities, in the southern part of the box, there are more implementing partners, however the remoteness, and sole dependency on supply chains from South Sudan (Sudan supply chains being disrupted) continue to present challenges including but not limited to the higher prices of commodities and transport fees. The Abyei AA is currently classified as IPC 4 , where the entire population needs some form of humanitarian assistance. Reaffirming its commitment to support the unprecedented efforts by the RCs/HCs in Sudan and South Sudan in joint implementation

title: Promotion of Solar Tuk Tuk for Public Transportation for Rural in Gedaref State
description: In rural Gedaref State, Sudan, transportation for people and agricultural goods relies on outdated petrol-powered three-wheelers and donkey carts, which are inefficient, costly, and environmentally harmful. Rising fuel prices and unreliable petrol availability make it difficult for farmers to access markets, often rendering trade unprofitable and limiting local economic growth. These challenges constrain value chains, increase post-harvest losses, and deepen rural poverty while contributing to environmental degradation through fossil fuel dependence.This project addresses these challenges by introducing solar-powered Tuk Tuks supported by community-based solar charging hubs to create an affordable, sustainable, and reliable transportation system. By replacing petrol-powered vehicles with solar alternatives, the project will enhance market access for farmers, reduce transportation costs, and generate new income opportunities for men and women through gender-responsive ownership and capacity-building programs. The solar charging hubs will also serve broader community energy needs, fostering resilience and self-sufficiency. By demonstrating the commercial viability of green transportation solutions, the project encourages private sector participation and presents a scalable model for clean rural mobility, advancing livelihoods, environmental sustainability, and inclusive economic growth.

title: Support National Medical Supplies Fund (NMSF) for Procurement of Life Saving Medicines
description: Since 2013, Sudan has been facing significant challenges in availing lifesaving medicines and health equipment. These difficulties are mainly due to a shortage of foreign currency and obstacles in the overseas processing of financial transactions required for global procurement.Since 2016, UNDP has supported the National Medical Supplies Fund (NMSF) in overcoming these challenges. This support includes capacity building for staff and the global procurement of essential medicines, which the government subsidises for populations in need.The overall objective of this Project is to further strengthen the national public health procurement and supply systems and thereby improve the effectiveness of diagnosis and treatment for patients in the Republic of the Sudan. The primary aim is to support public sector procurement of medicines, medical and laboratory equipment, supply chain equipment and consumables as required to enhance patient care in Sudan. The on-the-job collaboration between NMSF and UNDP will also help to build national technical capacities related to the supply of medical equipment.
